question: Which of the following places is the origin of river Indus?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bokhar Chu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indus River originates near the Bokhar Chu glacier on the Tibetan plateau, close to Lake Mansarovar and Mount Kailash. (सिंधु नदी का उद्गम — बोखार छू)

 

• It flows northwest through Ladakh, enters Pakistan, and finally drains into the Arabian Sea, running about 3,180 km, one of the longest rivers in Asia.

 

• Also known as Sindhu, it gave India its name and lent its name to the Indus Valley Civilization.

 

• Its major tributaries include the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej (left bank) and the Shyok, Gilgit and Kabul (right bank).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brahmaputra also rises near Mansarovar, from the Angsi/Chemayungdung Glacier area on the Tibetan side.

 

• The Ganga originates from the Gangotri Glacier (Gaumukh) in Uttarakhand.

 

NOTE

 

• Gangotri Glacier (Option 2): This is the source of the river Ganga (Bhagirathi), not the Indus.

 

• Chemayungdung Glacier (Option 3): This glacier near Mount Kailash is associated with the origin of the Brahmaputra, not the Indus.

 

• Zemu Glacier (Option 4): Located in Sikkim, it is the source of the river Teesta, not the Indus.

question: Who among the following Indian dancers was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2020 for contribution to Odissi dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabindra Atibudhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rabindra Atibudhi was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2020 for his contribution to Odissi dance. (संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार — रवींद्र अतिबुड़ी, ओडिसी नृत्य)

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, is India's national academy for music, dance and drama, and confers the highest national recognition on performing artists.

 

• The award carries a fellowship, a citation, and a monetary prize, recognising sustained career contribution to the art form.

 

• The Akademi Awards for the years 2019, 2020 and 2021 were announced together in 2022, owing to pandemic-related delays.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Odissi exponents honoured by the Akademi over the years include Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sanjukta Panigrahi and Sonal Mansingh.

 

• Odissi is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, native to Odisha.

 

NOTE

 

• Brajendra Kumar Pattnaik (Option 1): An accomplished Odissi artist, but not the confirmed 2020 awardee for this category.

 

• Balkar Sidhu (Option 2): A Punjabi singer/actor, unconnected with Odissi dance.

 

• Pasumarthy Vithal (Option 4): Associated with Kuchipudi dance, not Odissi.

question: The correct electronic configuration of Cu is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Copper (Cu, Z = 29) has the anomalous electronic configuration [Ar]3d¹⁰ 4s¹ instead of the 'expected' [Ar]3d⁹ 4s². (कॉपर का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास — [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹)

 

• This exception occurs because a fully filled 3d¹⁰ subshell provides greater stability (extra exchange energy) than a filled 4s with a partially filled 3d.

 

• Chromium (Cr) shows a similar exception: [Ar]3d⁵ 4s¹, gaining a half-filled, more stable 3d subshell.

 

• This behaviour is explained by Hund's rule/exchange-energy considerations, which favour symmetrical (fully filled or half-filled) subshells over partially filled ones.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Silver (Ag) and Gold (Au), lying below Cu in Group 11, show the same type of anomaly: [Kr]4d¹⁰ 5s¹ and [Xe]4f¹⁴ 5d¹⁰ 6s¹ respectively.

 

• Copper commonly exhibits +1 and +2 oxidation states in its compounds.

 

NOTE

 

• [Ar]3d⁹ 4s² (Option 1) and [Kr]3d⁹ 4s² (Option 2): Both follow the 'expected' Aufbau order without the 3d¹⁰ stability exception; Option 2 additionally uses the wrong noble-gas core (Kr, Z = 36, has more electrons than the whole Cu atom, Z = 29).

 

• [Kr]3d¹⁰ 4s¹ (Option 3): Has the correct 3d¹⁰ 4s¹ arrangement, but the noble-gas core should be [Ar] (Z = 18), not [Kr] (Z = 36).

question: క్రింది ఏ పండుగ ప్రధానంగా మణిపూర్‌తో ముడిపడి ఉంది? [Which of the following festivals is mainly associated with Manipur?]
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yaosang.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Yaosang (also spelt Yaoshang) is the major spring festival of Manipur, celebrated for five days from the full moon day of the lunar month of Lamta (February–March). (यावोसांग महोत्सव — मणिपुर)

 

• It coincides with Holi, blending the indigenous Yaosang tradition with the Krishna-centred Ras/Holi tradition introduced through Vaishnavism.

 

• It features Thabal Chongba (moonlight folk dance), Yaosang sports, and the burning of a thatched hut (Yaosang Mei Thaba), symbolising the destruction of a demoness, akin to Holika Dahan.

 

• It is one of the most important festivals of the Meitei community of Manipur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Manipur include Lai Haraoba (worship of Umang Lai/forest deities) and Kut (a harvest festival of the hill tribes).

 

• Thabal Chongba, performed during Yaosang, is a traditional group folk dance performed under moonlight.

 

NOTE

 

• Baisakhi (Option 2): A harvest and New Year festival mainly celebrated in Punjab.

 

• Wangala (Option 3): The post-harvest 'festival of hundred drums' of the Garo tribe of Meghalaya.

 

• Harela (Option 4): A festival marking the onset of the monsoon/sowing season, celebrated in Uttarakhand (Kumaon).

question: Which of the following statements is correct about the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution?
option_2: It has been borrowed from the Soviet Union
option_3: They are enumerated in Part II of the Constitution
option_4: Is described as ‘novel feature of the Constitution’
solution_text:
The correct answer is Is described as 'novel feature of the Constitution'.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution, were described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as a 'novel feature' of the Indian Constitution. (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — नवीन विशेषता)

 

• DPSP were borrowed from the Irish Constitution (which in turn drew on the Spanish Constitution), not from the Soviet Union.

 

• They are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts) but are declared 'fundamental in the governance of the country', guiding the State in policy-making.

 

• They aim to help establish a welfare state by promoting social and economic democracy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III (Articles 12–35) of the Constitution, distinct from DPSP.

 

• The Sapru Committee (1945) first suggested dividing rights into justiciable and non-justiciable categories, forming the basis of the FR–DPSP division.

 

NOTE

 

• Consists of Art. 12 to 32 (Option 1): This range corresponds to Fundamental Rights (Part III), not DPSP.

 

• It has been borrowed from the Soviet Union (Option 2): Incorrect — DPSP were borrowed from the Irish Constitution, not the Soviet Union.

 

• They are enumerated in Part II of the Constitution (Option 3): Incorrect — DPSP are in Part IV; Part II deals with Citizenship.

question: What is the state of matter that exhibits behaviour uniformity?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gas is the state of matter that exhibits uniformity of behaviour — all gases, irrespective of their chemical identity, tend to obey the same set of gas laws (Boyle's law, Charles's law, ideal gas equation) under similar conditions. (गैस — व्यवहार में एकरूपता)

 

• This uniform behaviour arises because gas particles are far apart with negligible intermolecular forces, so bulk properties (pressure, volume, temperature) depend mainly on the number of particles, not their chemical nature.

 

• In contrast, solids and liquids have significant, substance-specific intermolecular forces, so their properties (melting point, viscosity, etc.) vary widely and don't follow one universal law.

 

• The kinetic theory of gases models all gases as point particles in random motion, which is why their macroscopic behaviour converges to common laws such as PV = nRT.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• At very high pressure or very low temperature, real gases deviate from ideal behaviour, described instead by the Van der Waals equation.

 

• The ideal gas equation, PV = nRT, applies (approximately) uniformly to all gases under normal conditions.

 

NOTE

 

• Snow (Option 1): A solid form of water; does not show this kind of cross-substance uniform behaviour.

 

• Solid (Option 2): Solids have definite shape and strong, substance-specific intermolecular forces, so behaviour varies from one solid to another.

 

• Liquid (Option 3): Liquids have definite volume but no fixed shape, with intermediate intermolecular forces that also vary by substance.

question: At what temperature (in degree Celsius) is milk heated for 15 to 30 seconds to kill microbes in the pasteurisation method?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 70.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the flash/HTST (High Temperature Short Time) pasteurisation method, milk is rapidly heated to about 70–72°C (commonly cited as 71.7°C/161°F) and held for 15–30 seconds to kill pathogenic microbes while preserving nutritional value and taste. (पाश्चुरीकरण तापमान — लगभग 70 डिग्री सेल्सियस)

 

• Pasteurisation is named after the French scientist Louis Pasteur, who developed the process in the 1860s.

 

• The process reduces microbial load significantly but does not sterilise the milk completely, unlike UHT treatment.

 

• After heating, the milk is rapidly cooled to prevent further bacterial growth and preserve shelf stability.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The older 'Holder' (batch) method of pasteurisation heats milk to a lower temperature (~63°C) for a longer duration (~30 minutes).

 

• UHT (Ultra High Temperature) treatment heats milk to ~135–150°C for a few seconds, giving it a much longer shelf life.

 

NOTE

 

• 45 (Option 1): Too low to effectively kill pathogenic microbes present in milk.

 

• 100 (Option 2): The boiling point of water — far higher than the temperature actually used, and boiling would alter milk's taste and nutrition.

 

• 20 (Option 4): Near room temperature; far too low to kill microbes and would actually promote bacterial growth.

question: Which state’s governor approved the Prohibition of Online Gaming and Regulation of Online Games Bill 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Governor of Tamil Nadu gave assent to the 'Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Online Gambling and Regulation of Online Games Bill, 2022', which bans online gambling and regulates online games such as rummy and poker played for stakes. (तमिलनाडु ऑनलाइन गेमिंग विनियमन विधेयक — तमिलनाडु)

 

• The bill was passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly in October 2022, aiming to curb the negative social effects of online betting/gambling.

 

• It empowers the state to constitute a Tamil Nadu Online Gaming Authority to regulate online gaming platforms.

 

• The bill followed a spate of suicides linked to online gambling losses in the state, which prompted the government to act.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Several other states (e.g., Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana) also attempted similar bans on online betting/gambling around the same period, with mixed judicial outcomes.

 

• At the national level, the Central Government later enacted the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025.

 

NOTE

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 2): Had earlier passed its own online gambling ban ordinance/act (2020), but the specific 2022 bill in question belongs to Tamil Nadu.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): No such 2022 online gaming bill of this specific kind was enacted here.

 

• Punjab (Option 4): Regulates gaming under its Public Gambling Act but did not pass this particular 2022 bill.

question: In the Indian Constitution the concept of ‘equality before law’ is borrowed from the ____ constitution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is British.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The concept of 'equality before law' under Article 14 of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the British Constitution, rooted in A.V. Dicey's concept of the 'Rule of Law'. (विधि के समक्ष समानता — ब्रिटिश संविधान)

 

• The Rule of Law requires that no person is above the law and that everyone, including the government, is subject to the same law administered by ordinary courts.

 

• Article 14 guarantees 'equality before law' (a negative concept, from Britain) and 'equal protection of laws' (a positive concept, from the US).

 

• The British Constitution also inspired India's parliamentary system of government, single citizenship, and Cabinet system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• From the US Constitution, India borrowed Fundamental Rights, judicial review, and independence of the judiciary.

 

• From the Irish Constitution, India borrowed the Directive Principles of State Policy and the method of election of the President.

 

NOTE

 

• Canadian (Option 2): India borrowed a quasi-federal system with a strong centre and the concept of residuary powers from Canada.

 

• US (Option 3): Inspired 'equal protection of laws' (the second limb of Article 14) and Fundamental Rights generally, not specifically 'equality before law'.

 

• Irish (Option 4): Source of DPSP and nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha, not equality before law.

question: Gross primary deficit is equal to ____________.
option_1: difference between gross fiscal deficit and interest payments
option_2: difference between total expenditure and total receipts
option_3: difference between net borrowings and net capital receipts
option_4: difference between revenue deficit and capital expenditure
solution_text:
The correct answer is difference between gross fiscal deficit and interest payments.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gross Primary Deficit = Gross Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments. It measures the government's borrowing requirement excluding interest liabilities on past debt. (सकल प्राथमिक घाटा — राजकोषीय घाटा घटाकर ब्याज भुगतान)

 

• Gross Fiscal Deficit itself equals Total Expenditure minus (Revenue Receipts + Non-debt Capital Receipts).

 

• A zero primary deficit means the government borrows only to meet interest obligations, with non-interest expenditure fully financed by its own revenue.

 

• The primary deficit is used to assess the current fiscal stance, isolating the impact of past borrowings (interest burden) from the current year's fiscal effort.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts, indicating a shortfall on the government's current (non-capital) account.

 

• Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit − Grants for creation of capital assets.

 

NOTE

 

• Difference between total expenditure and total receipts (Option 2): This broadly (with adjustments) describes fiscal deficit, not primary deficit.

 

• Difference between net borrowings and net capital receipts (Option 3): Not a standard definition used for any recognised deficit measure.

 

• Difference between revenue deficit and capital expenditure (Option 4): Mixes unrelated deficit and expenditure categories; not the definition of primary deficit.

question: Who among the following Indian shuttlers has won the Silver medal in the u-17 women’s singles at Badminton Asia Junior Championship 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Unnati Hooda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Unnati Hooda won the silver medal in the U-17 girls' singles event at the Badminton Asia Junior Championships 2022, held in Jakarta, Indonesia. (बैडमिंटन एशिया जूनियर चैंपियनशिप — उन्नति हुड्डा)

 

• She became the first Indian woman to reach the U-17 singles final at this championship, losing to a Chinese opponent in the summit clash.

 

• Unnati Hooda, a young shuttler from Haryana, later created history by becoming one of the youngest Indians to win a BWF World Tour title (India Open 2024, women's singles).

 

• The Badminton Asia Junior Championships is an annual continental event for junior shuttlers organised by Badminton Asia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India won multiple medals at the 2022 edition, including a silver by Anish Thoppani (U-17 boys' singles) besides other medals in doubles events.

 

• Unnati Hooda featured in India's squad for the Uber Cup/Thomas & Uber Cup at a young age.

 

NOTE

 

• Amar Verma (Option 1), Aryan Shah (Option 2) and Abhishek Kiran (Option 4): None of these names correspond to the actual medallist in this event; the correct medal-winner is Unnati Hooda.

question: Which of the following was the capital of the Hindu Shahi kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Waihind.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Waihind (also known as Udabhandapura, present-day Hund, on the banks of the Indus in the Peshawar valley) was the capital of the Hindu Shahi kingdom. (हिन्दू शाही राजधानी — वैहिंद)

 

• The Hindu Shahi dynasty ruled the Kabul Valley, Gandhara and parts of Punjab from around the 9th century to the early 11th century CE, succeeding the Turk Shahis.

 

• Kings such as Jayapala, Anandapala and Trilochanapala of the Hindu Shahi dynasty famously resisted the invasions of Mahmud of Ghazni from this base.

 

• The dynasty was eventually defeated by Mahmud of Ghazni in the early 11th century, ending Hindu Shahi rule in the northwest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Facing repeated invasions, Hindu Shahi rulers later shifted parts of their base towards Punjab as Waihind came under increasing pressure.

 

• The Hindu Shahis built notable temples in the Kashmir-Gandhara style of architecture, including in the Salt Range.

 

NOTE

 

• Srinagar (Option 1): Capital of Kashmir under various dynasties (e.g. Karkota, Lohara), not the Hindu Shahis.

 

• Lahore (Option 2): Became important later in Punjab's history, but was not the original Hindu Shahi capital.

 

• Multan (Option 4): An important medieval city/kingdom in its own right, not the Hindu Shahi capital.

question: Pandavani Folk singer ______ is a Padma Bhushan Awardee of 2003.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Teejan Bai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Teejan Bai is a renowned exponent of the Pandavani folk-singing style of Chhattisgarh, narrating episodes from the Mahabharata centred on the Pandavas. (पंडवानी लोकगायिका — तीजन बाई)

 

• She was awarded the Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2003), and later the Padma Vibhushan (2019) for her contribution to Pandavani.

 

• She also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1995) and is credited with popularising Pandavani nationally and internationally.

 

• Pandavani is traditionally performed in either the 'Vedmati' style (seated, with a tanpura) or the 'Kapalik' style (standing, more theatrical) — Teejan Bai is known for the latter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Pandavani singers include Ritu Verma and Jhaduram Devangan.

 

• Chhattisgarh's other important folk art forms include Raut Nacha and Panthi dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Sulakshana Pandit (Option 1): A Bollywood playback singer, unrelated to Pandavani.

 

• Mamta Chandrakar (Option 3): A well-known Chhattisgarhi folk/playback singer, but not the 2003 Padma Bhushan awardee for Pandavani.

 

• Ila Arun (Option 4): A Rajasthani/Bollywood folk singer and actress, not associated with Pandavani.

question: Which of the following players won Silver at the Tokyo Olympics 2020?
option_3: Ravi Kumar Dahiya and Mirabai Chanu
option_4: Ravi Kumar Dahiya and Sushil Kumar
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravi Kumar Dahiya and Mirabai Chanu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021), Mirabai Chanu won silver in women's 49 kg weightlifting, and Ravi Kumar Dahiya won silver in men's 57 kg freestyle wrestling. (टोक्यो ओलंपिक रजत पदक — मीराबाई चानू, रवि कुमार दहिया)

 

• These were India's only two silver medals at the Games.

 

• India's overall medal tally at Tokyo 2020 was a then-record 7 medals: 1 gold, 2 silver, 4 bronze.

 

• Sushil Kumar did not compete at or win a medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020; his Olympic medals came from 2008 (bronze) and 2012 (silver).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Neeraj Chopra won India's only gold medal at Tokyo 2020, in the men's javelin throw.

 

• India's four bronze medals came from PV Sindhu (badminton), Lovlina Borgohain (boxing), the Indian men's hockey team, and Bajrang Punia (wrestling).

 

NOTE

 

• Mirabai Chanu and Sushil Kumar (Option 1): Sushil Kumar did not medal at Tokyo 2020.

 

• PV Sindhu and Sushil Kumar (Option 2): PV Sindhu won bronze, not silver, at Tokyo 2020, and Sushil Kumar won no medal here.

 

• Ravi Kumar Dahiya and Sushil Kumar (Option 4): Dahiya's silver is correctly listed, but the actual second silver medallist was Mirabai Chanu, not Sushil Kumar.

question: In which session of the Indian National Congress was the resolution declaring Poorna Swaraj passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lahore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The resolution declaring 'Poorna Swaraj' (complete independence) as the goal of the Indian National Congress was passed at the Lahore Session of the INC, held in December 1929, under the presidency of Jawaharlal Nehru. (पूर्ण स्वराज प्रस्ताव — लाहौर अधिवेशन, 1929)

 

• The Tricolour flag was hoisted on the banks of the Ravi River at midnight on 31 December 1929, and 26 January 1930 was subsequently observed as the first 'Purna Swaraj Day'.

 

• This marked a turning point from the Congress's earlier demand of Dominion Status to complete independence from British rule.

 

• It set the stage for the Civil Disobedience Movement launched by Gandhi in 1930 (the Dandi March).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• 26 January was celebrated as Independence Day by the Congress every year from 1930 until 1947; after independence, the date was retained for Republic Day (1950).

 

• The 1928 Calcutta Session had earlier given the British government a one-year ultimatum to grant Dominion Status, failing which Poorna Swaraj would become the goal.

 

NOTE

 

• Calcutta (Option 1): The 1928 session demanded Dominion Status with a one-year deadline, not Poorna Swaraj itself.

 

• Bombay (Option 2): The 1934 Bombay session dealt with other organisational resolutions, not the Poorna Swaraj declaration.

 

• Madras (Option 3): The 1927 Madras session saw an unsuccessful attempt (moved by S. Srinivasa Iyengar) to adopt complete independence as the goal; it was formally adopted only at the 1929 Lahore session.

question:
With reference to Manipuri classical dance which of the following statements is correct?

a) Lai Haraoba is the earliest form of Manipuri dance.

b) Ras, Sankirtana and Thang-Ta are the most popular forms of this dance.

c) Manipuri dance has its origin in the Jain traditional dance form.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both a and b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement (a) is correct: Lai Haraoba, a ritual festival-dance honouring local deities (Umang Lai) of the indigenous Meitei religion, is regarded as the earliest form from which Manipuri dance evolved. (लाई हराओबा — मणिपुरी नृत्य की प्राचीनतम शैली)

 

• Statement (b) is correct: Ras Lila, Sankirtana, and Thang-Ta (a martial art form) are among the most popular and recognised forms/components associated with Manipuri dance.

 

• Statement (c) is incorrect: Manipuri dance is rooted in the indigenous Lai Haraoba tradition and later assimilated the Vaishnavite Ras Lila tradition (especially under King Bhagyachandra in the 18th century); it does not originate from the Jain tradition.

 

• Manipuri Ras dances are characterised by gentle, flowing movements, soft footwork, and elaborate traditional costumes (e.g. the Kumin/Potloi skirt).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nata Sankirtana of Manipur, a devotional performance combining singing, drumming (pung) and dance, was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2013.

 

• Manipuri is one of the eight recognised classical dance forms of India, along with Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Kathakali, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.

 

NOTE

 

• a, b, c (Option 1): Incorrect because statement (c), on Jain origin, is factually wrong.

 

• Both a and c (Option 2): Incorrect — it includes the wrong statement (c) and excludes correct statement (b).

 

• Both b and c (Option 4): Incorrect for the same reason — it wrongly includes (c) and excludes correct statement (a).

question: According to David Ricardo, during a high deficit situation taxation and borrowing are ____ means of spending.
solution_text:
The correct answer is equivalent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to David Ricardo's proposition — later formalised as 'Ricardian Equivalence' by economist Robert Barro — taxation and government borrowing are equivalent means of financing government spending, especially during periods of high fiscal deficit. (रिकार्डियन तुल्यता — कराधान और उधार समतुल्य)

 

• The idea is that if a government finances spending through borrowing instead of current taxes, rational forward-looking individuals anticipate the future taxes needed to repay that debt and save accordingly, so aggregate demand is unaffected either way.

 

• Thus, whether the government taxes now or borrows now (implying taxes later), the economic impact on the public's spending/saving behaviour is essentially the same.

 

• This proposition is a foundational (though widely debated) concept in public finance and macroeconomics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Critics of Ricardian Equivalence point out that it may not hold fully in the real world due to factors like liquidity constraints, finite time horizons, and myopic behaviour of taxpayers.

 

• The concept is closely linked to debates on the sustainability of fiscal deficits and public debt.

 

NOTE

 

• Prudent (Option 1): Not the term used to describe the relationship Ricardo drew between taxation and borrowing.

 

• Differentiated (Option 2): Incorrect — Ricardo's point was precisely that they are not fundamentally different in economic effect.

 

• Subsidised (Option 4): Not related to the Ricardian equivalence concept.

question: According to Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, What was the percentage of population living below the poverty line in Chhattisgarh in the year 2004-05?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 40.9%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per data released by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, the percentage of population below the poverty line in Chhattisgarh in 2004-05 was 40.9%. (छत्तीसगढ़ में गरीबी रेखा से नीचे जनसंख्या — 40.9%, 2004-05)

 

• This figure reflects the combined (rural + urban) poverty ratio for the state for that reference year.

 

• Poverty estimation for this period was based on methodology recommended by expert groups (such as the Lakdawala Committee, later revised by the Tendulkar Committee).

 

• Chhattisgarh, a largely tribal and mineral-rich state carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000, has historically had poverty levels above the national average.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subsequent estimates (e.g. Tendulkar Committee's 2011-12 figures) showed declining poverty ratios in most Indian states, including Chhattisgarh, compared to 2004-05 levels.

 

• The national average poverty ratio for 2004-05 (Uniform Recall Period) was estimated at around 37.2%.

 

NOTE

 

• 35.9% (Option 1), 32% (Option 3) and 49% (Option 4): These do not match the officially reported combined poverty ratio of 40.9% for Chhattisgarh in 2004-05.

question: At the Sportstar Aces Awards in 2023, which state received the prize for the best state for sports promotion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the Sportstar Aces Awards 2023, Odisha was honoured with the 'Best State for Promotion of Sports' award, received by Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik. (स्पोर्ट्सस्टार एसेस पुरस्कार — ओडिशा, सर्वश्रेष्ठ खेल प्रोत्साहन राज्य)

 

• This was the fourth time Odisha won this award, reflecting the state's sustained investment in sports infrastructure and hosting of major events, such as the Hockey World Cup 2018 and 2023 (Bhubaneswar/Rourkela).

 

• The Sportstar Aces Awards, instituted by *Sportstar* (a publication of The Hindu Group), recognise excellence across Indian sports each year.

 

• Odisha has actively supported sportspersons and national federations (e.g., sponsoring Indian hockey teams) as part of its sports promotion strategy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other Sportstar Aces 2023 honourees included PR Sreejesh and Savita Punia (hockey), recognised for individual sporting excellence.

 

• Odisha built the Kalinga Stadium (Bhubaneswar) and Birsa Munda Hockey Stadium (Rourkela) as key sporting venues.

 

NOTE

 

• Punjab (Option 1): Known for producing many sportspersons but was not the 2023 recipient of this specific award.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): Has invested in sports infrastructure but did not receive this particular 2023 award.

 

• Haryana (Option 4): A major sporting talent hub, but not the awardee of this specific title in 2023.

question: ఏ పంచవర్ష ప్రణాళిక విడులైనప్పటి నుండి ప్రభుత్వ రంగానికి ప్రాధాన్యత తగ్గింది? [Since the release of which Five Year Plan has the priority given to the public sector reduced?]
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ninth Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Following the 1991 economic reforms (liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation), the Ninth Five Year Plan (1997–2002) marked a clear shift away from public-sector-led planning, emphasising private-sector participation, market-oriented reforms, and reduced state dominance in industry. (नौवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना — निजी क्षेत्र को प्राथमिकता)

 

• The Ninth Plan's central theme was 'Growth with Social Justice and Equality', focusing on employment generation, poverty alleviation and human resource development rather than expanding public sector enterprises.

 

• Earlier plans, up to the Eighth, had continued to give substantial emphasis to the public sector, especially heavy industries and infrastructure, in line with the Mahalanobis strategy.

 

• The reduced priority to the public sector, though it began with the Eighth Plan (1992-97) immediately after the 1991 reforms, is attributed as becoming markedly entrenched from the Ninth Plan onward.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97) was the first plan implemented after the 1991 reforms and focused on human resource development and modernisation of industries.

 

• The Planning Commission was eventually replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015, ending the era of Five Year Plans after the Twelfth Plan (2012-17).

 

NOTE

 

• Eighth Plan (Option 1): Initiated the post-1991 reform process, but the marked reduction in public-sector priority is attributed to the subsequent Ninth Plan.

 

• Eleventh Plan (Option 3): Focused on 'Faster and More Inclusive Growth', long after the shift away from public-sector dominance had already occurred.

 

• Seventh Plan (Option 4): Predates the 1991 reforms and continued the traditional emphasis on public sector-led growth.

question:
Which of the following is an objective of the Government Budget?

A) GDP Growth

B) Reallocation of Resources

C) Balanced Regional Growth
solution_text:
The correct answer is All – A, B and C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• GDP Growth (A): A key objective of the government budget is to promote a higher and sustained rate of economic growth through public expenditure, infrastructure investment, and fiscal incentives. (सरकारी बजट के उद्देश्य — आर्थिक संवृद्धि, संसाधनों का पुनः आवंटन, संतुलित क्षेत्रीय विकास)

 

• Reallocation of Resources (B): Through taxes, subsidies, and public expenditure, the budget helps reallocate resources between private and public use, and towards priority/welfare sectors.

 

• Balanced Regional Growth (C): The budget also aims to reduce regional disparities by directing funds towards the development of backward regions and states.

 

• Other recognised objectives of the government budget include reducing income/wealth inequalities, ensuring economic stability, and managing public enterprises.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The government budget is presented annually under Article 112 of the Indian Constitution as the 'Annual Financial Statement'.

 

• Fiscal policy tools used to achieve these objectives include taxation, public expenditure, and public borrowing.

 

NOTE

 

• Only A (Option 1), Only A and C (Option 3), Only B (Option 4): Each under-selects the objectives — GDP growth, reallocation of resources and balanced regional growth are all recognised objectives of the government budget, so any option excluding one or more of A, B, C is incomplete.

question: Which organisation formerly known as the Imperial Council of Agricultural Research and founded on July 16, 1929, is in charge of Agricultural Research and Education in India?
option_2: Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA)
option_3: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ICAR, established on 16 July 1929 as the Imperial Council of Agricultural Research (renamed in 1946), is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare responsible for coordinating agricultural research and education in India. (भारतीय कृषि अनुसंधान परिषद — ICAR)

 

• It is headquartered in New Delhi and oversees a nationwide network of agricultural research institutes, universities, and Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs).

 

• ICAR played a pivotal role in the Green Revolution in India during the 1960s, contributing to major advances in agricultural production and food security.

 

• It coordinates, guides and manages agricultural research and education across the country, spanning crop science, animal science, fisheries, and agricultural engineering.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• ICAR's premier institutes include the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI, Pusa, New Delhi) and the National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI, Karnal).

 

• ICAR also runs the Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) scheme to transfer agricultural technology directly to farmers at the district level.

 

NOTE

 

• Food Corporation of India – FCI (Option 1): A statutory body handling procurement, storage and distribution of foodgrains, not agricultural research.

 

• APEDA (Option 2): Promotes export of agricultural and processed food products, not agricultural research/education.

 

• NABARD (Option 3): The apex development bank providing credit for agriculture and rural development, not a research/education body.

question: Which of the following states has the National Academy of Sciences?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Academy of Sciences, India (NASI), founded in 1930, is headquartered in Prayagraj (Allahabad), Uttar Pradesh. (राष्ट्रीय विज्ञान अकादमी — प्रयागराज, उत्तर प्रदेश)

 

• NASI is the oldest science academy in India and works to promote scientific research and disseminate scientific knowledge across the country.

 

• It regularly publishes scientific journals/proceedings and confers fellowships and awards on Indian scientists for outstanding contributions.

 

• It should not be confused with the Indian National Science Academy (INSA), headquartered in New Delhi, or the Indian Academy of Sciences (IASc), headquartered in Bengaluru.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has three major national-level science academies: NASI (Prayagraj), INSA (New Delhi), and IASc (Bengaluru).

 

• Uttar Pradesh is also home to other major scientific/educational institutions such as IIT Kanpur and BHU (Varanasi).

 

NOTE

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 1): Home to institutions like the Wildlife Institute of India and Forest Research Institute (both in Dehradun), not NASI.

 

• Telangana (Option 2): Hosts institutions such as CCMB and NGRI (Hyderabad), not the National Academy of Sciences.

 

• Karnataka (Option 4): Home to the Indian Academy of Sciences (IASc) and Indian Institute of Science (Bengaluru) — a different body from NASI.

question: Name an oval-shaped range of hills sculpted by glacial flow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Drumlins.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Drumlins are oval/elongated, streamlined hills composed of glacial till (unsorted glacial debris), shaped by the movement of glacial ice; their long axis is aligned with the direction of ice movement. (हिमानी स्थलरूप — ड्रमलिन)

 

• They typically occur in groups referred to as a 'basket of eggs' topography, with a steeper, blunter end facing the direction the ice came from (stoss end) and a tapering, gentler end in the direction of ice movement (lee end).

 

• Drumlins are a depositional landform, distinguishing them from purely erosional glacial features like cirques or aretes.

 

• Notable drumlin fields occur in Ireland, parts of the UK, Canada, and the northern US — regions once covered by continental ice sheets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important glacial depositional landforms include eskers (long, winding ridges of sand/gravel deposited by meltwater streams within/under glaciers) and moraines (accumulated glacial debris/till at the margins or base of a glacier).

 

• Erosional glacial landforms include cirques, horns (e.g., the Matterhorn), aretes, and U-shaped glacial trough valleys.

 

NOTE

 

• Sandur (Option 1): A term for a flat plain formed by glacial outwash sediments, not an oval-shaped hill.

 

• Moraines (Option 3): Ridges/mounds of unsorted glacial debris deposited at the edges/base of a glacier, distinct from the specific oval-shaped, streamlined hill landform described here.

 

• Esker (Option 4): A long, sinuous ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams, not an oval-shaped hill.

question: విభిన్నమైనదానిని గుర్తించండి. [Identify the odd one out.]
option_4: జారీ చేసే సంస్థ యొక్క హామీ [Guarantee of the issuing institution]
solution_text:
The correct answer is Intrinsic value (అంతర్గత విలువ).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fiat money is currency that a government has declared to be legal tender, but it is not backed by a physical commodity such as gold or silver — its value derives from government order/decree, not from intrinsic worth. (फिएट मुद्रा — आंतरिक मूल्य का अभाव)

 

• Characteristic features of fiat money include: it is a legal proposition (declared legal tender by law), it is 'ordered' money (its value is fixed by government order), and its value is guaranteed by the issuing authority (e.g., the central bank/government).

 

• 'Intrinsic value' refers to the inherent worth of the material a currency/commodity is made of (e.g., a gold coin's value from its gold content) — this is a feature of commodity money, not fiat money.

 

• Since fiat money's value rests entirely on government backing/public trust rather than the material it is made of, 'intrinsic value' is the odd one out among the listed characteristics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Examples of fiat money include modern currency notes and coins issued by central banks (e.g., the Indian Rupee issued by the RBI), which have negligible material/intrinsic value themselves.

 

• Commodity money (e.g., gold/silver coins) is the opposite case, where the money's value comes largely from the intrinsic value of the material used.

 

NOTE

 

• Legal proposition (Option 2): A genuine characteristic of fiat money — it is money by legal declaration/legal tender status.

 

• Ordered/fiat money (Option 3): This restates the defining nature of fiat money itself — money whose value is fixed by government 'order'.

 

• Guarantee of the issuing institution (Option 4): A genuine characteristic — fiat money's acceptability rests on the guarantee of the issuing authority.
